summary.text: McGovern is the incumbent and is unopposed on the November general-election ballot. A Worcester native and former longtime aide to Rep. Joe Moakley, he was first elected in 1996 and is Ranking Member of the House Rules Committee; he also serves on the Agriculture Committee and is co-chair of the House Hunger Caucus. His official biography emphasizes his work on hunger and human rights.

paragraphs.text: Born in Worcester, Massachusetts, and raised in the city's Burncoat neighborhood, according to his official biography; his parents own a small package store and his sisters are public school teachers.

Studied at American University in Washington, D.C.; Ballotpedia lists a bachelor's degree (1981) and a master's degree (1984), and his official biography says he earned a B.A. in history while working his way through college.

Began as a volunteer on Sen. George McGovern's 1972 presidential campaign as a seventh grader and later sought an internship in the senator's office while at American University, according to his official biography.
Worked for over a decade, 14 years according to Ballotpedia, as a senior aide to the late U.S. Rep. John Joseph Moakley (D) of South Boston.

In 1990, led the Moakley Commission's congressional investigation into the 1989 murder of six Jesuit priests, their housekeeper, and her daughter in El Salvador by the Salvadoran Army; the commission's report led to a change in U.S. foreign aid policy.
Ran for Congress in 1996 and has been reelected every two years since; he took office in 1997.
Has been the top Democrat on the House Rules Committee since 2018 and chaired it during the 116th and 117th Congresses, according to his official biography.
Serves on the House Agriculture Committee, where his office says he worked to secure a White House Conference on Hunger, Nutrition, and Health, and is co-chair of the House Hunger Caucus.

Serves on the Congressional-Executive Commission on China and the Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission; his official biography lists legislation he authored that became law, including the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act, the Tibet Policy and Support Act, and the Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Act.
According to his official biography, he is married to Lisa Murray McGovern and they have two children.
